supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40 UTC, a proxy request authenticated as NWD\ivy.chen retrieved https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1 with status 200.
The reported PowerShell-window time closely coincides with the retrieval, but the available records do not establish that the downloaded script was executed or caused the window.
The script path is under an organization-named GitHub repository, but the records do not establish whether the repository or script was authorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the script download but do not include its contents, hash, or repository authorization status.
The supplied records do not include a PowerShell process-creation event or PowerShell script-block/module logging that would confirm execution or reveal what the script did.
The evidence is a set of selected records; missing process or execution events in this set do not establish that no such events occurred.
claims_not_established: Whether u.ps1 was executed on WS-ICHEN-01.
Whether the script was legitimate, malicious, or an approved internal tool.
Whether the reported PowerShell window was caused by this download or by another activity.
Whether the script made changes, accessed data, or communicated with other systems.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the downloaded u.ps1 content and hash, and verify the repository, commit, and script against an authorized internal source or owner.
Collect endpoint process-creation and PowerShell operational/script-block logs for WS-ICHEN-01 around 13:40 UTC, including parent process, command line, and script content where available.
Check endpoint file/download artifacts and security-product telemetry to determine whether the script was saved or executed.
Ask ivy.chen whether she initiated the download or PowerShell activity and what task she was performing.
unrelated_findings: A Kerberos ticket request for sam.okafor originated from the WS-ICHEN-01 address, and WS-SOKAFOR-01 recorded a network logon for sam.okafor from that same address. This is outside the alerted 13:40 script activity and merits separate review against the stated remote-administration practice. (T033-00014, T033-00015, T033-00019)

Kerberos activity from the WS-ICHEN-01 address authenticated as leo.martins for WS-NBLAKE-01, followed by a network logon for leo.martins on WS-NBLAKE-01 from that address. Review separately; the records do not explain why this occurred. (T033-00237, T033-00238, T033-00249)

A Dropbox updater process ran on WS-ICHEN-01; Dropbox is not among the listed approved software or services. The records show the updater process, not a Dropbox file transfer. (T033-00210, T033-00211)

The proxy shows ivy.chen browsing to the AWS console and Slack, and a Webex process opening a Gmail URL. These services are not in the supplied approved-services list; this observation is separate from the PowerShell alert and does not establish data transfer or malicious activity. (T033-00212, T033-00222, T033-00232, T033-00276, T033-00280)
